question: If Trump loses Congress in November, what could his last two years look like?

lines.text: If Democrats win on 3 November, Trump's grip on Congress ends on 3 January. Here is what could come next.
First, the subpoenas. Democrats say they would investigate the Trump family's business deals and foreign gifts.
That includes the 400 million dollar jet from Qatar, being remodelled as Air Force One.
Impeachment is back on the table. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries will not rule it out.

scene.quote: We haven't ruled anything in, and we haven't ruled anything out in terms of impeachment

lines.text: But removal needs two thirds of the Senate. Last time, in 2020, he was acquitted.
Then the money fights. Government funding runs out on 11 December, and the debt ceiling is expected to hit in 2027.
Democrats have promised to repeal his tariffs, undo Medicaid cuts and end the Iran war.
So expect the veto pen. In his first term, Trump vetoed 10 bills, and Congress overrode just 1.
If the Senate flips too, his judges and cabinet picks need Democratic votes to be confirmed.
From 3 January: deals, or deadlock. And the clock runs to 2028.

sources.title: Trump impeachment is back on the table. Here's what Democrats could investigate if they win the House

caption: If Democrats win Congress in November, what changes for Trump's last two years? Investigations, impeachment talk, money fights and the veto pen. A scenario based on what each side has said, not a prediction.
